correctness.rationale: PASS: Every S-supported binary relation is an independent Boolean choice on exactly \(k^2+2k+2\) stabilizer orbits; the least-support meet law makes deletion-event inclusion-exclusion exact. For equivalences, fresh atoms must be either a single infinite block or distinct singleton blocks; the two cases force the \(H_k(d)\) partition census. The Bell consecutive-ratio estimate and first/second moments of the distinguished giant block and singleton blocks prove both limits, including convergence in probability. A standalone checker independently exhausts \(k\leq5\) equivalence partitions and every \(k\leq3\) binary orbit-table choice; finite tests are supporting checks, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: PASS: Context minimization for nominal semantic relations depends on which named atoms are genuinely necessary. The exact support spectrum gives a complete natural invariant for all finite contexts, and the asymptotic contrast shows that the same binary arity has opposite generic behavior under equivalence axioms. The logarithmic loss law is stronger than a mere zero-one support probability; it calibrates typical redundant names without claiming an algorithmic speedup or a broader theorem outside equality symmetry.
